message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade counter-offer in Monopoly.

I'm p4 with $553 cash after paying $200 income tax. I own several properties including MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, NEW_YORK_AVENUE, PARK_PLACE, and three with one house each. Several others are mortgaged.

p2 has a pink monopoly with houses and two get-out-of-jail-free cards. p3 has light-blue hotels, all four railroads, green properties with four houses each, and cash of $922. The original offer was $200 plus Mediterranean for Kentucky and Indiana. p2's counter demands $300 plus Mediterranean for those same two mortgaged reds.

Rejecting this offer is the right move. It would hand p2 $200 plus Mediterranean Avenue, which I must never give away, and would not complete my red set since Illinois belongs to p3. The light-blue hotel stretch remains the immediate threat. I will not sweeten the deal and will end the turn.

I need to roll from Income Tax next. The surrounding properties are all hotels or railroads, so I cannot afford to lose $300 and leave myself with only $253.

I am weighing whether to counter the offer instead of rejecting it. p2's pink monopoly is a smaller threat than p3's hotels, and their two get-out-of-jail-free cards could be useful.

I should not give p2 cash, since they only have $79 and that would help them survive and build more pink houses. Mediterranean Avenue is especially dangerous to give away because p3 already owns Baltic, and anyone who receives it could trade it to p3 for a brown monopoly with hotels. Buying the mortgaged reds for $300 plus Med is strictly bad for me. I am now trying to figure out what would actually help me win.

p3 is the dominant threat and will likely bankrupt both p2 and me unless we cooperate to hurt them. I cannot complete an orange monopoly because p2 holds St Charles with three houses. I have a dark blue set but Boardwalk is mortgaged, and unmortgaging it would cost about $242.

Unmortgaging Boardwalk costs $220, which is too risky with only $553 cash. I will reject the counter offer and continue playing to win.

I will reject the counter and keep my public message brief and non-confrontational. I considered offering alternatives, but p2's St Charles is too heavily developed to trade, and Water Works is not worth much. I will not sweeten the deal.

I will tell p2 the $300 price is too high for two mortgaged reds that cannot form a set, and that Illinois is locked with Gemini. I will not mention my cash worries or that Mediterranean is my emergency mortgage buffer.

The probability breakdown confirms the danger. Rolling a 3 or 8 lands on a $550 hotel, while rolling a 6 lands on a $600 hotel. With only $253 after paying $300, I cannot afford either hit and would be forced to mortgage Boardwalk or declare bankruptcy.

Mortgaging New York Avenue and Park Place would raise about $275, but that still leaves me with only about $530 after paying the $300 counter offer. That is not enough to survive a $550 hit on St Charles.

Selling houses to survive a hotel hit would leave me completely exposed to p3. I will reject the counter and may waste an exchange by offering nothing for the reds.
